You don't deserve that armor.|Maximus criticizing [[Titus]]|sound=Maximus.ogg}} '''Maximus''', originally '''Max''', is a member of the [[Brotherhood of Steel]] chapter known as the [[Knights of San Fernando]] {{In|FOTV}}. He is one of the three main protagonists, the other two being [[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]] and [[The Ghoul]]. During his childhood, he was known as '''Max''',{{FOTV|2|2}} though the extended name of Maximus was given to him by the Brotherhood. Maximus is a rookie soldier who grew up above ground but, like Lucy, was also raised in a cloistered "family" of sorts: the Brotherhood of Steel. However, unlike Lucy, he has a cynical sense of self-preservation and does not always act honorably. In [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], at the start of the TV series, Maximus is elevated to the rank of [[Brotherhood of Steel ranks#Squire|squire]]. He is sent by the Brotherhood with his [[Knights|knight]] as an expendable assistant. His mission leads him towards an [[Cold fusion|artifact]] from an enigmatic researcher called [[Siggi Wilzig]], causing his path to collide with those of Lucy and the Ghoul.[https://web.archive.org/web/20240314103018/https://press.amazonstudios.com/us/en/original-series/fallout/1 ''Fallout'' Season 1 description on Amazon Studios (archived)] ==Background== [[File:FOTV Official Trailer Still 058.png|thumb|left|200px|Max survives the bombing of Shady Sands as a child]] A former citizen of the [[New California Republic]] born in [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2277|2277]], Max had the misfortune of living in [[Shady Sands]]. The NCR's capital [[Fall of Shady Sands|was destroyed]] with a nuclear weapon when he was 6 years old. Although he was on the edge of the crater, he survived thanks to his father [[Joseph (TV series)|Joseph]], who placed him inside a refrigerator in their house; his father and his mother [[Julia (TV series)|Julia]] both perished in the blast. After leaving his hideout, Max saw the still-burning crater and charred bodies of other NCR citizens before coming face to face with an [[:File:Shady Sands Knight and Maximus.png|armed Brotherhood knight]] in [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|power armor]]. The memory was seared into his mind, defining the trajectory of his life. [[File:Shady Sands Knight and Maximus.png|thumb|200px|Maximus found by a Brotherhood knight]] Orphaned in the nuclear attack, the boy was taken to the Knights of San Fernando's [[Brotherhood base|base and training camp]] in [[New California]]. He was given a new name, Maximus, as well as food, shelter, education, and a chance to rise through the ranks of the Brotherhood.[[Quintus|Elder Cleric Quintus]]: ''"We have given you a name. Food. Education. A place in the world. So... we expect you to give us the truth. Why did you join the Brotherhood?"''
Maximus: ''"To hurt the people who hurt me."''
({{FOTV|1|1}}, 50:20) From the outset, he was an outsider, targeted by [[Thaddeus]] for bullying. It wasn't personal for Thaddeus, just a matter of deflecting the abuse Thaddeus was receiving onto a new, more attractive target. This gambit worked, and so Maximus became the underdog.[[Thaddeus]]: ''"Bet you, uh, seen some things, huh? Being a knight. I've seen some things. I grew up working on a fly farm. I was a shitter, so they'd feed us, and then they'd feed our shit to the flies. Mulch 'em up and sell it as protein. Anyway, that's why I'm so fat. So, your, uh, former squire, how did he die?"''
Maximus: ''"You knew him?"''
Thaddeus: "''Yeah, I... I did."''
Maximus: ''"Say something about him."''
Thaddeus: ''"Well, he, uh, he was a good guy."''
Maximus: ''"Say something negative about him."''
Thaddeus: ''"Well, uh, he-he's dead. I don't know, it feels weird."''
Maximus: ''"An order, my squire."''
Thaddeus: ''"Okay. Uh, to be honest, me and the other guys used to be pretty hard on him. Like, regularly beat the shit out of him. It wasn't personal, you know. It's just... well, you know, people at the base, they used to beat the shit out of me all the time. This shipment of new recruits came in, and, uh, one of them was Maximus. So I had this funny idea, what if we beat the shit out of that guy instead? And it worked. Yeah, I was really popular. It was great. I just wish he'd lived long enough to find someone else to beat up, you know? Only seems fair. I realize that, uh, people die all the time. It's the law of the Wasteland, so who cares, right? But still, uh, I feel bad."''
Maximus: ''"Don't feel bad. It's like you said, it's the law of the Wasteland. Let's go. We're losing daylight."''
({{FOTV|1|3}}) Shunned by most of his fellow aspirants, he became close friends with only one: [[Dane (TV series)|Dane]].{{fotv|1|1}} While he developed an impressive physique and endurance, allowing him to withstand regular beatings and even strike back at the bullies, he struggled with more cerebral subjects. In particular, technical and scientific subjects proved challenging, earning him the ire of [[cleric]]s teaching the subjects, such as [[Felix (TV series)|Cleric Felix]].[[Felix (TV series)|Cleric Felix]]: ''"It is the duty of the Brotherhood of Steel to secure the Wasteland. One day as squires, you will help knights find and identify prewar tech. Aspirant Maximus. Can you identify this relic?"''
Maximus: ''"It's a... rotor?"''
Cleric Felix: ''"A circuit. The ability to defend yourself is but one part of your training. We are the finders and the preservers. Unless you know what to find and preserve, you are more useful as a corpse."''
({{FOTV|1|1}}) Despite that, he persevered, hoping to one day be able to hurt those who hurt him, like those who destroyed Shady Sands. The Brotherhood earned his loyalty and Maximus developed a steadfast belief in its mission and values, not yet tempered by the reality of the wastelands or the Brotherhood's method of operation. It is his sincere belief that "a knight's duty [is] to better this fallen world."Maximus: ''"It is a knight's duty to better this fallen world. You don't deserve that armor."''
[[Titus|Knight Titus]]: ''"Oh, you think you do? You fuck. They'll kill you for this. You..."''
Maximus: ''"Not if I bring back the target."''
({{FOTV|1|2}}) However, his lack of life experience makes him prone to hasty decisions and mistakes, some of them very consequential. Due to his traumatic childhood and hard life in the Brotherhood, some of these gaps have left him unaccustomed to creature comforts, unaware that humans can still enjoy a good quality of life in the post-apocalypse.{{fotv|1|6}} The biggest gap in his experience is tied to sex. The Brotherhood does not have a sexual education curriculum, and so Maximus is not entirely familiar with the concept of intercourse, ejaculation, or masturbation. He is actually somewhat repulsed by sex, either believing or excusing himself by claiming that Brotherhood knights are supposed to be celibate.Maximus: ''"You smell good."''
[[Lucy MacLean]]: ''"What? Oh. You want to have sex?"''
Maximus: ''"You mean use my cock?"''
Lucy MacLean: ''"Yeah."''
Maximus: ''"I don't know. Uh, that weird thing could happen."''
Lucy MacLean: ''"What weird thing?"''
Maximus: ''"Well, it's just, for some guys... not me... uh, but for some guys, you know, when they make it move, it gets all big and hard like a big pimple and then it pops. And they say it can happen to anybody, but it's still, it's... it's gross."''
Lucy MacLean: ''"You know, that's... uh, that's actually completely normal. It happens all the time. Every time, ideally."''
Maximus: ''"I'm a knight. Um, a knight of the Brotherhood. We're-we're not supposed to."''
Lucy MacLean: ''"Okey dokey."''
({{FOTV|1|6}}){{fotv|1|2}}{{fotv|1|3}}{{fotv|1|5}}{{fotv|1|7}}{{fotv|1|8}} ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== {{Quotation|When Maximus’s family and community were taken from him in a traumatic incident as a child, he was raised by the Brotherhood of Steel. They became his family and community. His biggest fear is weakness and he seeks power as a means to shield himself from the violence and dangers of the Wasteland.|[[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 1 character description]]}} ====[[The End (episode)|The End]]==== [[File:FOTV Season1 ep1 Minions.png|thumb|250px|Maximus being physically assaulted]] Maximus is beaten up by Thaddeus and his group of [[Thaddeus' minion|"minion" aspirants]] at the Brotherhood base, seemingly for no other reason but bullying. Once the group leaves, chased away by the arrival of some [[Brotherhood officer|officers]], Dane arrives to check on Maximus' condition. One day, Dane is promoted to [[Brotherhood of Steel ranks|squire]] instead of Maximus, which frustrates Maximus. However, Dane's foot is maimed while getting out of bed, causing suspicion to fall upon Maximus. [[File:FOTV Official Trailer Still 059.png|thumb|250px|left|Maximus being interrogated about Dane]] Maximus is escorted into a repurposed aircraft by [[Shortsight|Petty Officer Shortsight]], where he is to be interrogated by [[Quintus|Elder Cleric Quintus]] and a Brotherhood knight who intimidates Maximus to speak truthfully. When Quintus questions Maximus why he joined the Brotherhood of Steel, Maximus says, "To hurt the people who hurt me." Quintus informs Maximus that his fellow aspirants have accused him of orchestrating Dane's maiming. Maximus denies it, but Quintus asks him if he has the ambition to advance in the Brotherhood and why he would not desire such an outcome on a rival. Maximus admits that he did want Dane to be injured so he could take their spot, but he maintains that he did not do it. Quintus lectures Maximus that violence against a fellow brother is a sign of weakness and asks Maximus if he is weak. Maximus replies that he doesn't want to be. When given a chance to give any statements in his defense, and feeling that his defense may not be enough to be found innocent, Maximus thanks the Brotherhood for his guidance, giving him a home and a place in the world. Maximus looks at Quintus and says: "If I can help the Brotherhood make it [the world] better... Eden or whatever... even if it means giving my own life... I'll do it. And I'd be grateful to the Brotherhood for giving my life meaning." Impressed by Maximus' character, Quintus believes his defense, clearing him of these charges, and promotes him to be [[Titus|Knight Titus]]' squire in Dane's place. [[File:FOTV BoS Base Clinic.png|thumb|250px|Maximus visits Dane in the camp clinic]] Afterward, Maximus checks on Dane at the medical tent. Dane reassures Maximus that their circumstances aren't so bad. When Maximus asks if they suspect anyone of causing their injury, Dane replies they've narrowed it down to any of their bullying peers. Dane informed Maximus that they knew he took their spot, and they both confirmed that they'd both been questioned about whether there was any credibility to the rumor that Maximus was the perpetrator of Dane's maiming. Dane, however, tells Maximus that they told their interrogators that they believed that Maximus wouldn't hurt a fly. Maximus and Knight Titus are assigned the mission of searching for [[Siggi Wilzig]], a member of the [[Enclave]] on the lam, who also has an object that can change the balance of power in their nation. ====[[The Target]]==== [[FIle:Maximus and Titus.webp|thumb|250px|left|Maximus with Knight Titus]] Maximus soon learns that Knight Titus is callous and a bully since he would order Maximus to perform demeaning work, such as cleaning his codpiece. While en route to their ordered destination of [[Filly]], Titus spontaneously orders the [[vertibird]] they were flying in to drop them off midflight because he is bored and wants to kill something. Despite straying from their objective, Titus and Maximus stumble onto one of Wilzig's camps near a [[yao guai]]'s cave. Despite Titus being better equipped to handle a Yao Guai, Titus orders Maximus to delve deeper into the Yao Guai's den ahead of him, only for the Yao Guai to sneak behind Titus and attack. Maximus was frozen in shock as Knight Titus was overwhelmed by the Yao Guai, and after being disarmed by the Yao Guai, Titus fled the cave in terror until he tripped and smashed his head on a rock. The Yao Guai proceeded to maul Titus until Maximus composed himself and shot the Yao Guai dead. Titus orders Maximus to remove his helmet, then ruthlessly insults and blames him for his sustained damages. Titus reveals he is contemptuous of the Brotherhood of Steel's purpose and his superiors; he complains of being sent to face the dangers of the [[wasteland]] for a "toaster oven." Titus orders Maximus to fetch him a [[stimpak]] and threatens Maximus with a torturous death for failing his duties as a squire. Maximus judges Titus antithetical to the Brotherhood's purpose of bettering their fallen world and deems him unworthy of his power armor. Thus, Maximus withholds the stimpak from Titus. Although Titus threatens Maximus by saying that the Brotherhood would kill him, Maximus asserts he won't be punished if he returns with the target. Maximus then watches Titus die of his wounds. Maximus takes Titus' power armor and assumes his identity. While playing with the power armor and testing its capabilities, Maximus interrupts a scuffle between a [[chicken collector]] and a [[snake oil salesman]]. Maximus used the strength of his power armor to subdue the attacking chicken collector, while the snake oil salesman smugly escaped. Maximus then learned that the reason the chicken collector was attacking the snake oil salesman was because he was having sex with the chicken collector's chickens. Maximus was perturbed by such strange behavior but acted as if the matter was resolved satisfactorily. [[File:FOTV First Scene Still 012.png|thumb|250px|Maximus about to fight The Ghoul]] When Maximus arrives at Filly, he finds that The Ghoul has shot up the town to obtain the bounty on Wilzig and that Lucy MacLean has stood up to The Ghoul to protect Wilzig. Maximus intercedes to shield Lucy from being shot by The Ghoul and tells Lucy that Wilzig is important to him and that he will cover their escape by keeping The Ghoul busy. Maximus' power armor could throw The Ghoul around the town for a while, but The Ghoul used the heavy weight of the armor and the fragility of the town's structure to outmaneuver Maximus. Maximus gets his foot stuck on a fragile platform, immobilizing him. The Ghoul mocks Maximus' inexperience with piloting the power armor and advises him to read its manual before going around him and using his knife to break some of the armor's components. This causes his power armor to malfunction, and although he escapes his immobility by attempting flight, Maximus' malfunctioning suit causes him to fly clumsily. Coupled by The Ghoul using a towing cable to rope Maximus and disrupt his flight pattern, Maximus loses control; he flies and crash-lands somewhere out of the town. Nevertheless, his distraction allowed Lucy to escape town with Wilzig. ====[[The Head]]==== [[File:FOTV s1 ep3 Jamila haggles.png|thumb|250px|left|Jamila refuses to repair the component because Maximus is short a single cap]] After the confrontation with The Ghoul, Maximus's power armor is damaged. He tows his power armor to a nearby stand. As he's checking its condition (finding a damaged component while doing so), Petty Officer Shortsight talks over the radio, attempting to check up on Knight Titus' condition after having missed a check-in. Maximus deepens his voice and pretends to be Knight Titus. He lies to the Brotherhood by telling them that the squire assigned to him (Maximus) had died while in a confrontation with an "abomination"; however, his plan goes wrong as the other party suggests sending a replacement squire. Maximus tries to convince them not to send one, as this would blow his cover. After failing to convince the Brotherhood not to deliver a replacement squire, he intentionally destroys the power armor's radio to cut off communications with the Brotherhood. Afterward, Maximus goes to a local repair stand to have the aforementioned damaged component repaired. [[Jamila]] mentions he is one cap short, which he compensates for by selling his tooth. [[File:FOTV Filly unconscious man.png|thumb|250px|Maximus fighting off a raider]] As he checks in on his power armor, he discovers a group of bandits attempting to take it apart. He attempts to defend his property; however, he is initially overwhelmed by their superior numbers and beaten down. Maximus quickly recovers, grabs iron tongs and a toilet seat for melee weapons, and confronts the bandits again. He manages to knock two of them out, and is nearly defeated when he is pinned to his power armor by the remaining two and beaten; however, he manages to activate the power armor's right arm, crushing one of the bandits' heads with it. The other bandit is scared away by the brutal display. As he breathes a sigh of relief, a Brotherhood [[vertibird]] flies over the town, delivering [[Thaddeus]] as the replacement for Maximus as a squire. Before his replacement squire can notice, Maximus returns to his power armor and hurriedly enters it to hide his identity. Initially, Maximus contemplated killing Thaddeus, but ultimately decided to use him as a squire and bully him for his amusement. Repeating his former knight's actions, he orders Thaddeus to clean his power armor's codpiece. Thaddeus relays information about the fact that they "are not the only ones looking for the target," and is told by the Brotherhood to kill anybody that stands in their way. After leaving [[Filly]], Maximus continues to demean Thaddeus, ordering him to climb a dead tree and look for apples, even though there are obviously none. Thaddeus falls to the ground, much to Maximus's amusement. Thaddeus suggests repairing the power armor's radio to contact the Brotherhood for reinforcements, to which Maximus gets mad and tells him that he will retrieve the target by himself. Afterward, they continue searching for the target. Maximus tells Thaddeus about his encounter with The Ghoul. Thaddeus approves of his knight's idea to let The Ghoul live since all wastelanders carry radiation, which they can trace. Maximus takes credit for this idea, even though he had never considered it. While following The Ghoul's trail, they stumble upon the rest of Wilzig's headless body. They mistakenly credit the decapitation to be The Ghoul's doing. Thaddeus suggests retrieving the rest of the body, but Maximus thinks the body is useless to them, as whatever was valuable about Wilzing must have been in his head. On a short break while on their journey, Thaddeus attempts to refill the power armor's water bag, to which Maximus gets startled and pushes him away. After realizing Thaddeus was trying to fulfill his duties as a squire, he sits down and allows him to refill it. The two of them converse, with Maximus asking him about his thoughts on Knight Titus' apparently dead squire (himself). Thaddeus starts off by talking positively about him, but Maximus orders him to say something negative about him. He discovers that Thaddeus had only been bullying him because he had been bullied before Maximus' arrival and wanted to redirect the bullying on him instead, making him popular. Thaddeus comments that he wished Maximus had lived long enough to redirect the bullying on someone else himself. Maximus begins to empathize with Thaddeus. [[File:FOTV Official Trailer Still 093.png|thumb|250px|left|Maximus facing the gulper]] Afterward, they continued following the tracks of The Ghoul, leading them to Hollywood Boulevard, which had been flooded with radiated water and inhabited by a [[gulper]]. Maximus rebuked Thaddeus for leading them to danger but ordered him to run to safety while he personally dealt with the Gulper. While attempting to take the creature down, Maximus runs out of ammo from his pistol and prepares to fight in close-quarter combat; Thaddeus, however, aids him and shoots at the Gulper with a rifle. However, this alerts the gulper to Thaddeus' location, and he is chased down and dragged by the beast. The gulper nearly swallows Thaddeus, but Maximus comes to aid Thaddeus by grabbing him and pulling him out of the beast's mouth from the opposite side. The tug of war causes the gulper to vomit and die. While recovering from the situation, they find the target (Wilzig's head) to be among the things the gulper vomited and being licked by [[CX404]], who had been searching for Wilzig as well. They celebrate at the sight of this and prepare to return the head to the Brotherhood. ====[[The Past]]==== [[File:The Past Maximus and Thaddeus.png|thumb|250px|Maximus and Thaddeus]] Maximus and Thaddeus are camping for the night at an abandoned rail station. The two banter and reminisce about their epic battle with the gulper. Thaddeus gets the idea for Knight Titus to brand him, unaware that the man in the power armor is actually Maximus. Maximus hesitates at first, but eventually agrees to do it reluctantly after some coaxing from Thaddeus. After branding him, Maximus reveals his identity and opens the faceplate of his power armor, revealing himself. Thaddeus is shocked, but Maximus tries calming him down by proposing they can still be friends. However, he needs Thaddeus to corroborate a made-up story that will help Maximus avoid punishment from the Brotherhood. Thaddeus is reluctant to participate in his scheme, fearing that the Brotherhood will find out Maximus killed his knight and also get him in trouble. Maximus reacts to this with immense disappointment and stands up, telling Thaddeus that he knew "he should not have trusted him"; afterward, he attempts to attack Thaddeus. Maximus can crush Thaddeus' foot, but he manages to avoid being killed due to Thaddeus' mobility advantage compared to his bulky power armor. In the ensuing fight, Thaddeus uses his master key to turn off Maximus' power armor and steals its [[Fusion core (TV series)|fusion core]], leaving Maximus trapped in the power armor. Thaddeus takes the head and departs, leaving Maximus to be trapped in his armor and die alone. [[File:FOTV Maximus POV.png|thumb|250px|left|Maximus's view from his power armor as Lucy approaches him]] The next morning, Maximus, still trapped, is swarmed by [[radroach]]es. Frightened, he watches as the radroaches nearly eat through his power armor. He survives this encounter after the radroaches are shot down by Lucy MacLean, who opens up his faceplate and recognizes Maximus as the knight back in [[Filly]]. Maximus begs her to open his power armor and let him out, telling her someone had stolen his fusion core, but Lucy hesitates to free him. She asks if he remembers [[Siggi Wilzig|the man she left with]], who Lucy describes as "with the glasses and the whole body." Maximus is aware of Wilzig as he is also searching for him. Lucy then informs him that she, too, is looking for his head. Lucy starts to vomit, which Maximus diagnoses as radiation sickness. He tells her that he has [[RadAway]] in his sleeve and that she can have it if she lets him out. Lucy is once again hesitant, telling Maximus that practically every person she has met on the surface has attempted to kill her. Maximus once again tells her that they would die if she did not let him out. When Lucy asks for his name, he lies to her by telling her that his name is Knight Titus. Lucy then opens up Maximus' power armor and frees him. Lucy correctly identifies the model of Maximus' power armor as the [[T-60 power armor|T-60]], which she recalled that the [[United States of America|U.S.]] [[United States Army|Army]] started using them after the [[Battle of Anchorage]]. She comments that she had only seen them in old engineering manuals and never in real life. Lucy suddenly faints and is caught by Maximus. She wakes up sometime after Maximus administers RadAway to her. He comments that he had never known that people lived in [[Vault]]s. Lucy asks him what he thinks are in the vaults, if not people, to which Maximus replies with "monsters." Lucy responds by telling him that the rumor he heard is incorrect, and that the vaults are inhabited by "regular folk like her." Maximus says that his "squire" stole "something vital" to the Brotherhood, and that he has to go after him. He attempts to depart, before Lucy stops him. She tells him she has a tracker that will lead them straight to the head, which she correctly assumes is what Maximus is looking for. She offers to travel together with him and to catch up to Thaddeus with her tracker, retrieve the head, and return it to the Brotherhood; in exchange, the Brotherhood will lend her "five or six" knights who will assist her in rescuing [[Hank MacLean|her father]]. Maximus is reluctant at first, but is reassured by Lucy that he can trust her. Lucy claims that vault dwellers like her are honorable and that she comes from a place where the worst anyone can do to someone is "forget to say thank you." Maximus comments that it sounds like a nice way to live, with Lucy reaffirming his sentiment. They both shake hands on their deal and depart together. As they walk down a railroad line, Lucy asks Maximus to give her history of the last 200 years. She claims that she knows about the [[Great War]], the bombs falling, and the 320 years of American history before then, yet she needs help with the last 200 years "after the bombs fell." Maximus responds that the bombs fell when he was a kid, to which Lucy asks if that's what they tell him in the Brotherhood. Maximus responds by saying that she is the one who grew up in a box underground. He also teases Lucy about her encounter with The Ghoul in Filly, asking if she really thought she would just "show up to some warlord, with no armor, no help, and expect him to just turn over a hostage to her," and asks her if she really thought that would work. Lucy responds by saying that she had the head, to which Maximus says that they don't even know what's in it, and Lucy concedes that he has a point. Lucy tells Maximus that she comes from a place where "the world is what you make of it," that it is not like the surface and that they are really naive down there; adding that up until she was six years old, she really thought "the big light" on their farm in [[Vault 33|the vault]] really was the sun. She additionally adds that [[Rose MacLean|her mom]] used to take her out to play under the sunlight. She swears that she could actually feel the sun, but states that after her mom was gone, she realized that it was just her mom's presence that made it feel real. She then asks Maximus if they (presumably referring to surface dwellers) think the Earth is round or flat. The duo encounters two weary-looking travelers opposite them while attempting to cross a rail bridge. With both groups distrustful of each other's intentions, Maximus asks Lucy to give him her gun, but she refuses. Lucy then offers a peaceful solution: both groups would simultaneously cross the bridge with their hands up. Midway through the crossing, however, the travelers shoot at them. Maximus reflexively grabs Lucy's gun from her gun holster and shoots both of them dead. However, he was shot and wounded in his left arm when he returned fire. After inspecting the travelers' corpses, Maximus reveals their attackers are members of the [[Fiends]]. Lucy asks him what a Fiend is, and Maximus tells her they are cannibals. The two of them eventually arrive at [[Shady Sands]]. Lucy, puzzled, looks at the town's welcome sign. Maximus asks her what she is confused by. Lucy questions the sign's content, asking Maximus for confirmation on whether it is real. Confused, Maximus asks her if she had never heard of the [[New California Republic]], to which Lucy, even more confused, asks if 34,000 people really lived in the city after the War. Maximus confirms it and tells her he used to be one of them. This seems to contradict the entire purpose of "Reclamation Day," which she realizes is meaningless since the entire purpose of her vault was to come up to the surface one day and restart civilization; that is what kept all of them going. After thinking about it, she sadly said it had already happened without them. In an attempt to make her feel better, Maximus replies that it didn't work out. [[File:FOTV Shady Sands Blast Crater.png|thumb|250px|Lucy and Maximus overlooking the crater left by the nuclear blast in Shady Sands.]] He then directs her to follow him, leading her to a massive crater in the city, from a nuclear blast. Maximus says that it's "always the same thing that happens," and that "everybody wants to save the world, they just disagree on how." After recalling childhood flashbacks, of which he hid in a refrigerator during the bombing of Shady Sands and was found by a Brotherhood knight, Maximus tells her that they should keep moving. Lucy stops Maximus to check on his wound, only to discover he has lost a sizable amount of blood. Seeing the severity of it, she comments that they have to find supplies to treat his wound. She leads Maximus to [[Hawthorne Medical Laboratories]], a pre-War subsidiary of [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]]. Maximus hesitates to enter, citing his worries that anything could be in there. Lucy enters anyway without him, which prompts Maximus to follow her in. After entering, Maximus is confused as Lucy is nowhere to be seen. Above him, a series of blinking lights are leading him in a direction, which he follows; he attempts to get into medical supplies, but discovers that the handle of the door leading to it is just a decal. He attempts to get out, but finds out that the door behind him is locked, and in a panic, he screams for Lucy's help. The room is then filled with sleeping gas, and a trap door below him opens, leading him into [[Vault 4]]. Lucy and Maximus wake up inside an isolated room in the vault. When Maximus asks where they are, Lucy replies by telling him they are in a safe location and he'll be alright. When Maximus asks what the place is, Lucy tells him they are in "the best place in the world," a vault. ====[[The Trap]]==== Maximus is treated by the [[Vault 4]] doctors, who tell him he needs a couple of days to recuperate before he's safe for travel. Although Maximus says he's fine so they can return to their quest, the doctors assert that he is in no condition to travel. [[Birdie]], one of the Vault's leaders, insists Lucy and Maximus stay at the vault to recuperate and even have their surface foragers retrieve Maximus' power armor, which is being kept in the vault for safekeeping. Lucy and Maximus are taken to stay in a quarantine room for a few hours to ensure that they don't track in any contamination into the Vault. While in quarantine, Maximus mentions to Lucy that she smells good. Noticing that Maximus is attracted to her, Lucy invites Maximus to have sex with her. Having never received any sex education, Maximus grew up being afraid to use his genitals, as he came to believe that sexual responses like arousal and ejaculation were likened to a pimple popping and were considered weird. Lucy reassures him that such sexual responses are completely natural and even encouraged. Even so, Maximus shyly said the Brotherhood of Steel wasn't supposed to participate in such activities. Later, Maximus and Lucy eat breakfast at the cafeteria. Maximus suspects the vault dwellers are trying to trap them and urges them to leave. Lucy trusts them since a lot of them are survivors of Shady Sands. She also reminds Maximus that he needs time to recuperate, so they can't leave. Maximus accuses Vault 4 of being a cult since they are all so happy and content, yet Lucy argues they are that way because the vault is a safe place and the people there look out for one another—especially since they all recognize that they need each other. Lucy holds Maximus' hand and likens the intimate bond of the vault dwellers to the one they have with each other. Lucy is later introduced to [[Overseer]] [[Benjamin (TV series)|Benjamin]], who only has one eye. When she notices that many of the vault dwellers have [[mutations]], Lucy becomes suspicious of them, although Maximus seems more concerned by their happy behavior than their physical differences. [[File:The Radio Maximus popcorn.png|thumb|250px|left|Maximus unwinds while enjoying his Vault room]] After discovering that a fusion core powers Vault 4, Maximus attempts to steal it to power his power armor. During his attempted theft, he is interrupted by Birdie, who says that he may be having trouble adjusting to a safe environment as he has been conditioned to think that the cutthroat lifestyle needed to survive the surface is the only norm. She gives Maximus access to his own room, Unit 428, and advises him to enjoy its comforts to aid in his transition. Maximus experiences the luxurious comforts of vault life for the first time and finds it pleasing. When Lucy visits him at his unit, he excitedly shows Lucy all the comforts he has indulged in and even awkwardly consents to her earlier invitation for sex. However, Lucy had just witnessed the vault dwellers perform a strange ritual and now thinks they are insane. Maximus downplays Lucy's fear and tries to find excuses to remain in Vault 4. Lucy tries to persuade Maximus that although life in Vault 4 may be more appealing than the horrors of the surface, she is certain that the vault dwellers are hiding something nefarious from them and will prove it to him. ====[[The Radio]]==== [[File:The Radio Vault 4 fight.png|thumb|250px|Due to misunderstanding the situation, Maximus attacks the Vault 4 dwellers]] Maximus continues to enjoy the comforts of his unit until he sees Lucy being carried away by the vault dwellers for some offense she has committed. At that moment, Maximus resolves to rescue Lucy and leave the vault together. Maximus steals Vault 4's fusion core and uses it to fuel his power armor. After equipping his armor, Maximus interrupts Lucy's trial and demands that the vault dwellers release her. Maximus begins to manhandle the vault dwellers and destroy their property until Lucy stops him and explains that they were releasing her to the surface and were being helpful to do so. Surprised by this information, Maximus embarrassingly apologizes to the vault dwellers and advises them to check on the people he just attacked. Maximus leaves the vault with Lucy and his power armor, but Lucy stops them to mention that without Vault 4's fusion core, Vault 4 can only survive on auxiliary power for a few days. Lucy thinks they should return the fusion core, but Maximus is reluctant to do so because without it, his power armor would be useless, and he wouldn't be able to be a heroic knight or help Lucy rescue her father. Lucy argues that her father wouldn't want to be rescued at the expense of innocent people. Ultimately, Maximus and Lucy return the fusion core to Vault 4 together. Lucy tells Maximus that he is the best stranger she has ever met and that he is a good person. After rescuing her father, she invites Maximus to live with her in [[Vault 33]]. Maximus discloses that he isn't really Knight Titus and reveals his real name to her. He explains that Knight Titus was a person he let die because he was threatening him and took his armor for himself afterward, and so admits he isn't the good person she believes him to be. Lucy admits that she threw acid at an innocent man's face during her investigation of Vault 4, and she has only been in the wasteland for two weeks. She chooses not to hold Maximus' past against him and invites him to live with her in her vault again. This time, Maximus happily accepts. [[File:Lucy Maximus kiss.png|thumb|250px|left|Lucy and Maximus' farewell kiss]] Maximus and Lucy eventually catch up to Thaddeus at the KPSS radio station in Hollywood Hills. As the two approach Thaddeus, Thaddeus shoots at them but misses every shot. Maximus and Lucy approach him peacefully with their hands up and explain they only want the head. Thaddeus steps on one of the traps littered throughout the radio station and gets a crossbow bolt lodged in his neck. Surprised that he hasn't died, Thaddeus takes out the crossbow bolt, only for his wound to be instantaneously healed. Maximus suspects that Thaddeus may be turning into a [[ghoul]], causing Thaddeus distress as the Brotherhood of Steel will surely kill him now. With the Brotherhood already en route to him, Maximus instructs Thaddeus to give him the head, and he'll return to the Brotherhood to slow them down so Thaddeus can escape to safety. Thaddeus thanks Maximus and gives the two abrupt apologies and farewells. Maximus then gives Lucy Wilzig's head so she can use it to free her dad and go home, while he takes a disfigured, fake head from a [[critic|nearby corpse]] and passes that one off as Wilzig's head to the Brotherhood. Although Lucy is reluctant to leave Maximus, they kiss and part ways. She tells Maximus to find her and to seek out Vault 33 someday. ====[[The Beginning]]==== Maximus is transported to Filly, which the Brotherhood of Steel has recently conquered. Once there, he is brought before Quintus, who notes that he is wearing Knight Titus' clothes. Maximus reveals that Knight Titus is dead and presents Quintus with the fake head. Quintus has his clerics examine the head, and they discover it's a fake since it doesn't have the artifact. Quintus accuses Maximus of lying about the artifact, as he lied about his culpability in Dane's maiming. The Brotherhood knights restrain Maximus and point a gun to his head, with Quintus demanding he confess. Maximus implores Quintus to spare his life, promising to lead the Brotherhood to the artifact's location if they do so. Dane then interjects, confesses that their injury was self-inflicted, and pleads for Quintus to listen to Maximus for the sake of the Brotherhood. Quintus commends such a rare display of loyalty and orders the knights to release Maximus. Quintus and Maximus have a private talk, where Quintus asks Maximus about the circumstances of Titus' death to which the squire coldly reveals that Titus died running. Seemingly unsurprised by this revelation, Quintus disappointedly admits that the Brotherhood had lost its way before reminiscing about when they ruled the wasteland on the West Coast. He adds that power must be taken and not given, which is a lesson that he believes Maximus has learned and experienced well. He continues by saying that by leading the Brotherhood to the relic, the two of them will be able to take power, allowing them to start a new Brotherhood, with Quintus as its leader and people like Maximus as its sword. He then reminds Maximus about his lifelong search for a home and offers him a chance to build one together. Maximus prepares to fight at [[Griffith Observatory]] and thanks Dane for speaking in his defense. Maximus is surprised to find that Dane will be fighting alongside him. Dane explains it's punishment for maiming themself and apologizes to Maximus for their deception, as they had no idea he would be blamed for it. Maximus tells Dane there's nothing to apologize for as he believes he was meant to go on that mission, elaborating that he met Lucy because of it. He's not only going to fight the upcoming battle to rescue her, but also to leave with her to live in her vault. Maximus describes her vault as a "... place that's peaceful... and safe. Where nobody ever goes to war." Dane replies that there is nowhere that's safe, and there is no leaving the Brotherhood, even though they wish there were. [[File:FOTV s1 ep8 Maximus during Ghoul fight.png|thumb|right|250px|Maximus and squadmates watch the Ghoul decimate their fellows]] Maximus fights in the [[Battle of Griffith Observatory|battle to take the observatory]]. After defeating [[Lee Moldaver]]'s [[New California Republic|NCR]] forces in the courtyard, during which Maximus shoots at least one [[NCR soldier (TV series)|NCR soldier]], Maximus' squadron breaches the observatory. Once inside the observatory, Maximus' squad is ambushed by the Ghoul and suffers heavy casualties; only Maximus is shown to escape, and the others' fates are left unseen. One of the knights the Ghoul decapitates inadvertently breaks through the control room doors where Lucy and her father, [[Hank MacLean]], are being held. Maximus enters the room, frees Lucy's father from his cage, and proceeds to try to shepherd Lucy to an escape from the battle. Lucy stops him as she refuses to return with her father, who she reveals was responsible for the bombing of Shady Sands. Enraged by this information, Maximus attempts to attack Hank, but Hank has equipped the fallen Brotherhood knight's power armor and knocked Maximus out. When Maximus regains consciousness, he notices that Lucy and her father have disappeared, Lucy having chosen to leave with the Ghoul to pursue Hank. Moldaver, who was grievously injured by gunfire during the battle, arrives to activate the artifact and uses it to create [[cold fusion]]. With the cold fusion reactor activated, Maximus and Moldaver watch as it powers [[Boneyard|Los Angeles]] with unlimited energy. Moldaver insinuates that the Brotherhood of Steel will abuse the unlimited energy that they will acquire after the battle. She warns Maximus about what the Brotherhood would do with unlimited energy and entreats him to try stopping them if they are corrupted by their newfound power, but is uncertain if he will succeed. Ultimately, she concludes that his trying is all anyone can expect of him. Moldaver succumbs to her wounds and dies. Dane finds Maximus with Moldaver's corpse and asserts that he killed her. Maximus attempts to correct Dane, but they have already started spreading the narrative to the rest of the Brotherhood forces present and begin calling for Maximus to be promoted to Knight Maximus for the feat. Hailing Maximus as a hero, the Brotherhood forces begin chanting for all to hail "Knight Maximus," though he is no longer happy about it like he may have been in the past. ===Season 2=== {{Quotation|Orphaned by the tragic bombing of his birthplace, Maximus is motivated by a yearning to belong and joins the militaristic Brotherhood of Steel. His commitment and loyalty help him rise quickly in rank, making the cracks in the Brotherhood’s seemingly altruistic missions and methods all the more visible.|[[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 2 character description]]}} ====[[The Golden Rule]]==== Maximus has a flashback to his childhood, remembering the day he lost his parents and his home upon the destruction of [[Shady Sands]] in [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2283|2283]]. In the present, in his new station as the highest-ranking knight of the San Fernando chapter, he leads a two-man mission with a fellow knight as both storm a [[Shadowy facility|shadowy pre-War facility]] in T-60 suits, eliminating several [[Feral ghoul (TV series)|feral ghouls]] to obtain a [[control panel]]. Returning to the ''[[Caswennan]]'', Maximus is welcomed by the celebrations of his chapter and meets with Quintus on the flight deck as he commends him on his success in retrieving "the key to [the Brotherhood's] new home." While scribes work with the control panel, Quintus tells Maximus his belief that the present-day Brotherhood lacks the strength to unite the wasteland due to the isolation and factionalism separating its many individual chapters; he intends to reunify these chapters with the Knights of San Fernando at the lead, first by carrying out their latest mission to obtain "the mightiest arsenal in history." The ''Caswennan'' arrives at an abandoned playground, where two scribes work with a [[Dirigible squire|squire on the flight deck]] to reactivate a dormant array of wind turbines that rise up from their underground siloes and blow away the immense layer of sand covering the structure underneath, revealed to be the pre-War military base of [[Area 51]]. Quintus tries to reinforce Maximus' trust in the Brotherhood's future, emphasizing they are going to make better their "fallen world" and referring to him as "[his] son." Maximus smiles in response to this comment, seeming to trust Quintus. On the ground at Area 51, an exploratory group of the Knights of San Fernando including Maximus enters the central warehouse to explore and begin uncovering its contents, with Maximus at one point reprimanding [[Riley (TV series)|Knight Riley]] for playing hot potato with a plasma grenade. Maximus later oversees the setup of the cold fusion technology, transported to Area 51 from its previous location at Griffith Observatory, as Dane observes him from afar and grows concerned about Quintus' motives. Maximus goes to wash his face in the barracks, helped by a [[young aspirant]] whom he in turn tries to mentor with his take on the Brotherhood's philosophy. Once alone, Maximus tries to polish his T-60 suit, lingering on the claw marks left by the [[Yao guai (TV series)|yao guai]] attack that killed its previous wearer, [[Titus]]. He is interrupted by Dane, who questions their friend about his recent shift in focus and how he is now helping the Brotherhood progress and especially adhering to the tenets of the [[Codex]], which they both once regarded as a joke. Maximus counters that he has realized the struggle of living in the wasteland and now feels he has to make the Brotherhood better. Dane brings up his former goal to have a life with Lucy MacLean, but Maximus says she abandoned him and now he has to fulfill his duties as a Brotherhood knight. Dane drops the matter and changes to the subject of a meeting that Quintus deliberately excluded the Commonwealth chapter from. Dane fears this will have serious repercussions, as the Commonwealth chapter would not let the elder cleric seize power without resistance. The base's alarms blare as Maximus assures his friend that he is going to do what he can to help the Brotherhood's mission if it means preventing another [[Great War|apocalypse]]. Outside the base, the San Fernando chapter witnesses the arrival of three other airships coming from various directions, carrying other chapters of the Brotherhood. Later on, all four chapters have assembled around a feasting table with Quintus and the three elders representing their respective chapters from the [[Grand Canyon]], [[Yosemite]], and [[Coronado]]. As Quintus props up their chances of defeating the Commonwealth now that his chapter has acquired the cold fusion technology and sways the elders to join his rebellion, Maximus is discreetly warned by Dane to stop [[Gnatius]] and another knight as they are playing with a plasma grenade like a toy. As the Brotherhood chapters celebrate their unification with a violent spectacle of two knights in T-60 suits boxing each other with the elders watching, Maximus, weary of the barbarism on display, tries to walk away but is intercepted by a [[Coronado knight|burly man]], one of the [[Coronado Brotherhood of Steel|Coronado chapter]]'s knights. The man asks if he was the one who dealt the killing blow to the "[[New California Republic|NCR]] bitch" [[Lee Moldaver|Moldaver]] (whom he refers to as "Mold Over"). Once Maximus confirms it, the knight challenges him to a fight of their own; Maximus tries to get Quintus to intervene, but the elder silently urges him to accept the challenge. Maximus' request to get his armor is rebuked with the knight stating they will be fighting "bareback:" no power armor, just fists and raw strength and skill. The two enter the ring formed by the crowd of onlookers, where the knight lands a cheap shot on Maximus while he is removing his jacket. Maximus is brutalized for a while, realizing nobody is going to intervene for him. He uses an opening to punch the knight's crotch, then throws his jacket in his enemy's face to stun him as he retaliates and kicks him back. The knight recovers and decides to increase the threat level by taking out a [[Combat knife (TV series)|combat knife]]. Maximus looks to Quintus again to stop the fight, but the elder leaves him to fend for himself. After dodging a few slashes, Maximus grapples with the knight and maneuvers him into stabbing himself in the abdomen. The two wrestle to the ground, where Maximus finally overpowers his opponent and fatally stabs the knight in the chest. Despite the cheers from the crowd, including the young aspirant from before, and Quintus giving silent approval, Maximus notices Dane giving him a somber gaze before turning and walking away. Right then, the celebration is interrupted by the arrival of a [[Vertibird (TV series)|vertibird]] as it flies directly into the warehouse and lands nearby. A man in a heavy coat jumps off and approaches the crowd, revealing himself to be [[Xander Harkness|Paladin Xander Harkness]], a liaison from the Commonwealth Brotherhood. He also reveals that the Commonwealth is aware of the West Coast Brotherhood's plans to start a civil war, which Quintus coldly acknowledges. Harkness then notices the bloodied Maximus standing over his fallen opponent and gives him an acknowledging nod, which Maximus returns. ====[[The Profligate]]==== in the aftermath of Harkness' arrival, Quintus fields a private meeting with his fellow [[cleric]]s and the [[Yosemite Brotherhood of Steel|Yosemite chapter]]'s [[McRae|Elder McRae]], with Maximus in attendance, where McRae reveals that the alliance of the four West Coast chapters has been shaken due to renewed fears of reprisal by the Commonwealth Brotherhood. The elder cleric tries to retain her allegiance by invoking the name and story of [[Roger Maxson]]'s rebellion against the pre-War U.S. that led to the Brotherhood's creation, but the Yosemite elder refutes him and declares her chapter is abandoning the alliance, citing the [[Codex]] and its prohibition of violence between brothers, and leaving after a final warning to hand over the cold fusion relic to the Commonwealth. In the silence after, Maximus also tries to use Roger Maxson's story to suggest that they eliminate Xander for their "righteous" cause, but Quintus mocks his shortsightedness since Xander's death would in all likelihood ignite war with the Commonwealth, then furiously dismisses him. As Maximus walks through the base, angered and conflicted by his thoughts, Xander calls out to him. The paladin remarks on the San Fernando chapter's abundance of clerics, and how his chapter does not use them in a leadership position. He then emphasizes to Maximus that Quintus' plans of rebellion will be nothing but chaos, for both the Brotherhood and the wasteland, and tries to sway the knight to his view of things, saying that soldiers like them, who understand the real cost of a battle, are the ones who lead back in the Commonwealth and make an example for the Brotherhood. Maximus expresses his uncertainty, but Xander reassures him, stating that the current situation is [[Schism|not the first time]] that the Brotherhood has faced civil war and made room for [[Arthur Maxson|"cooler heads"]] to step up and take command. Though Maximus remains reserved about his loyalty to his chapter, he agrees to discuss the topic more with Xander. Later, Maximus and Xander approach Xander's [[Vertibird (TV series)|vertibird]]. Maximus questions why they do not have a pilot, but Xander reveals he flies it himself. He offers to let Maximus use his spare suit of T-60 power armor, surprising Maximus that the Commonwealth chapter can grant its members spare power armor. During the flight over the wasteland, the two start talking as Xander lightens the mood by offering to let him take the controls of the vertibird, which the inexperienced Maximus declines. The conversation turns to the subject of Quintus' rebellion as Xander admits that if nothing is done to get him to turn over the relic, both of them will most likely be facing each other in battle in the future. He reveals to Maximus that his arrival was two-fold, as he also came to get the relic because it might prevent the Commonwealth chapter's own collapse back on the [[East Coast]]. Xander emphasizes to Maximus that he will have to be the one to make a choice, but he trusts Maximus' judgment and assures that Maximus himself must believe that too. They are alerted to the vertibird's sensors picking up the power signature of a nearby complex. Maximus wonders why Xander would care about that when it is happening far outside his home territory, but Xander rallies him by saying they have the obligation as members of the Brotherhood to protect the wasteland, which feeds into Maximus' idealism. The T-60-outfitted Xander and Maximus break into the complex with the power signature they tracked. As they get deeper, they stop upon hearing the stuttering, crackled voice of an [[extremely broken Securitron]]. The malfunctioning robot detects them and fires at them with its SMG arm, forcing the two into cover. Xander excitedly pulls out his [[Super sledge (TV series)|super sledge]], which Maximus does not recognize, and charges into the storm of bullets to attack it directly. The pair work together to disable the robot's weapons, allowing Maximus to punch his gauntlet through the Securitron's front screen and extract its [[Fusion core (TV series)|fusion core]]. As the two celebrate their victory and Xander offers the use of his super sledge to Maximus, they are drawn to a sound in a nearby room. They walk into the bottling floor housing Thaddeus' cap collecting operation, where Xander notices a [[ghoul]] child, [[Perry]], hiding under nearby machinery and demands he come out, then refers to him as a "baby abomination" upon seeing his mutated appearance. Seeing this, Maximus immediately starts to get uneasy, while Xander orders the rest of the children out of hiding. As the knight tries to reassure the scared children, Xander asks all the [[Smoothskin|"smooth skin"]] humans to move to one side of the room, separating them from the ghouls. Maximus immediately realizes Xander's intentions and tries to tell him to stand down. They are then interrupted by Thaddeus emerging from his hiding place as he tries to plead for the kids' safety, but Xander remains firm in obeying the [[Codex]] and eliminating the "abominations," including Thaddeus. Both Maximus and Thaddeus continue to beg Xander not to attack the children until Maximus makes the decision to swing the super sledge into the back of Xander's helmet, crushing it and killing him instantly. Maximus reveals himself to Thaddeus and laments that he just started a war. ====[[The Demon in the Snow]]==== Shortly after killing Xander, Maximus convinces Thaddeus to help him cover it up from the Brotherhood, right as a vertibird arrives that was tracking them. Despite initial reluctance, Thaddeus agrees to help after the knight points out the Brotherhood would discover the kids in the process of looking for him, killing the ghouls and recruiting the humans, if they did not create a distraction. Maximus exits the factory to meet Knight Gnatius, who blows off his excuse of Xander's vertibird running out of fuel and demands to know where the paladin is. Both look on as Thaddeus (disguised as Xander) fumbles trying to get through a normal-sized door, and Maximus sighs knowing how risky his plan is going to be. When the two are brought back to the airship's flight deck, Maximus is met by a worried Dane, who says Quintus is furious with Maximus for going off on his own with the Commonwealth's liaison. Dane then sees "Xander" awkwardly moving around in his power armor and deduces right away that something went wrong. Maximus confirms that he killed the real Xander and Dane wryly responds that the Commonwealth will most certainly be gunning for the West Coast chapters as a result, though Maximus claims he will resolve the situation. Though Dane warns him that Quintus will demand Maximus' death for killing Xander, Maximus responds by telling Dane to gather all of the aspirants in a safe place, as he intends to kill Quintus himself; this leaves Dane shocked. In the meeting room, Maximus is left alone with Quintus once the elder cleric dismisses his subordinates. He figures out that the incident with Xander went wrong, correctly deducing that the paladin was killed, which Maximus confirms, and that the knight intends to kill him too as Maximus draws his [[Laser pistol (TV series)|laser pistol]] and aims it at the elder cleric. Quintus is unfazed, walking right up to Maximus, who hesitates to shoot him, while lambasting the knight for his weak will and failure to think about what his actions would do to the Brotherhood and the future they are building, questioning the fearful Maximus what led him to turn against the man who brought him into the Brotherhood from the ruins of Shady Sands. Maximus, left agitated by Quintus' comments and the situation, confesses that he feels he has had no opportunity to make his own decisions, and that things simply keep forcing him to act, also admitting that he cannot make the kind of long-term plans that Quintus lambasted his shortsightedness for as a result. Quintus softens somewhat when Maximus admits this, and also after Maximus explains that he killed Xander to stop him from killing children. However, in his turmoil, Maximus then reveals the children were ghouls, which causes Quintus to angrily deride his subordinate for protecting "abominations" in defiance of the Codex's tenets, spitefully telling Maximus he should have never helped him, while Maximus continues to protest. The elder cleric draws a [[10mm pistol (TV series)|10mm pistol]] from a hidden drawer and tries to attack Maximus, loudly decrying him as a "heretic," but fails to hit him. Maximus returns fire with his laser pistol but also does not hit Quintus before escaping the room and chaining the door shut, trapping Quintus inside. In the hallway, Maximus realizes that war has already broken out as the chapters are fighting with each other. He sees Dane running in and reveals with sadness that he could not bring himself to kill Quintus, but Dane consoles their friend, saying he should not be sad over refusing to take a life. Dane reveals they stole the cold fusion relic that kicked off the surrounding battle and places it in Maximus' hands, telling him to take it and run far away from the Brotherhood. He hugs Dane and asks Dane what they will do; Dane tells him they'll survive like they always have. Maximus then leaves with Thaddeus; the two flee from the base with the relic in Maximus' hands as the airship fleet opens fire on each other and sends one crashing into the desert behind them. ====[[The Other Player]]==== After putting some distance between them and Area 51, Maximus has Thaddeus leave the power armor behind, telling him that the Brotherhood will be able to track it and find them. He considers what to do with the cold fusion diode in his hands, but rebukes Thaddeus' suggestion that they sell it as they start moving again. Later at night, around a fire in their makeshift campsite near some ruins, Thaddeus again suggests selling it off, but Maximus emphasizes giving it to the right person, a "good" person. Thaddeus refutes him on the idea of meeting good people in the wasteland, but Maximus cites Lucy as an example; Thaddeus remarks that it is easy to be a good person while growing up in the safety of a Vault and never needing to worry about scrounging for food and water nor having to resort to stealing, violence, and/or lying to get it in the first place. Maximus listens as Thaddeus explains how he connects his desire to sell the diode with the idea that the resulting wealth would give them the means to be "good." Thaddeus' final point is that, of all the "crazy" things he has seen in the wasteland, "good people" are not among them. Detecting that his friend is speaking from experience, Maximus asks where Thaddeus was born, and he reveals that he grew up in "the Shithole side" of the [[Boneyard]]. Maximus remarks that he was lucky to have grown up in [[Shady Sands]] among genuinely good people before Thaddeus jokes that if he is the lucky one between them, they are both screwed, which gets a laugh from Maximus. Sometime later, Maximus and Thaddeus are awoken by a bark coming from [[CX404|Dogmeat]], who brought with her [[the Ghoul]]'s hat. The two recognize her from previous encounters and follow after her. They eventually end up at the [[Mojave Mission School]] as the dog leads them into a shed. Maximus then reacts with shock to see the Ghoul inside, who similarly expresses his dislike for the "help" that Dogmeat found for him; Thaddeus just offers a friendly wave, to Maximus' confusion. ====[[The Handoff]]==== Maximus and Thaddeus follow the Ghoul to an [[Run-down town|abandoned NCR camp]], with Maximus still clutching the cold fusion diode in his hand. After Thaddeus fails to bond with the Ghoul, he asks Maximus about his previous encounter with the Ghoul (when they fought in Filly), and Max tells him that he was in power armor at the time. Thaddeus responds by mentioning his difficulties operating power armor back in Area 51, and asks Max if following the Ghoul is a good idea. Max reveals that they are doing so because the Ghoul said he would take them to Lucy MacLean. Maximus asks the Ghoul where they are going; the Ghoul tells them that their destination is the [[Lucky 38]]. When Thaddeus points out they are going the wrong direction, the Ghoul reveals that Lucy is being held in a [[Las Vegas management Vault|subterranean Vault-Tec facility]] underneath [[New Vegas]], and that they need to obtain weaponry in order to get past the [[Deathclaw (TV series)|deathclaws]] infesting the [[New Vegas Strip]]. However, Maximus, still digesting the previous information, just asks to confirm that Lucy is in New Vegas, which causes the Ghoul to snark about him and Lucy getting along due to them both frequently asking questions. In response, the Ghoul trains his revolver on Maximus and orders him to explain how he has the cold fusion diode, which the Ghoul was familiar with due to events involving cold fusion which he was involved in before the Great War. Though Thaddeus urges calm, Maximus holds his ground and does not explain, only putting the diode in his pocket and telling the Ghoul that he intends to give it to Lucy, whom he believes is a good person and will do the right thing with it. The Ghoul to respond with a slight smirk, but he seems to accept the answer, and they keep moving. Soon, the trio break into an abandoned NCR supply shack, still filled with crates of weapons, ammunition, and armor. While the others arm themselves, Maximus picks up a grenade launcher, though he does not keep it. Seeming confused, he turns and asks the Ghoul why he is offering them his help. The Ghoul reveals that he is actually bargaining with them: in exchange for getting the weapons and support needed to save Lucy, Maximus will have to give the Ghoul the cold fusion diode. Maximus walks up to the Ghoul, refusing to change his mind about giving the diode to Lucy and Lucy alone. However, the Ghoul explains that in order to save Lucy, the diode will have to be given to a "really bad person." He then alludes to [[Robert House]], the former executive of New Vegas and owner of the Lucky 38, saying that they will have to "rig the game" like he did in order to seize victory, before revealing a suit of [[Ranger power armor|NCR Ranger power armor]] under a tarp. Stunned, Maximus walks up to inspect the armor, brushing the cobwebs off of the NCR symbol on its chestplate. The sight makes him emotional, to the point of tearing up, as he realizes that he has "end[ed] up back where [he] started" in terms of donning the symbols of the NCR, his former home. This convinces him to hand over the diode to the Ghoul, and he begins to smile as he looks at the armor while the Ghoul walks away. Later, Maximus has equipped the NCR power armor, and he, the Ghoul, Thaddeus, and Dogmeat have returned to Freeside, where they walk down the main street towards the gate of the Strip. The sight of a figure in NCR armor causes the assembled [[Freesider|Freeside residents]] to express awe, shock, and respect; some even cheer, mistakenly believing that the NCR as a faction has returned. Maximus smiles as he passes by a young boy who gazes up at him with awe, just like he did as a child when [[Quintus]] rescued him from Shady Sands. The Freesiders follow the posse to the Strip gate, where they mentally prepare for the challenge inside. The Ghoul tells Maximus that they will have to move quickly, and orders Thaddeus to get into position for sniping; however, Thaddeus' arm suddenly falls off. Though Thaddeus believes he can still help, Maximus tells him to stay back due to his unexpected issue, and they leave him behind as they enter the Strip. Inside the Strip, the Ghoul tells Maximus to protect him from any deathclaws that they encounter; Maximus is immediately forced into melee combat against a deathclaw just in front of them. After steeling himself, Maximus sharpens the bladed forearm attachments on his power armor before he and the deathclaw charge at one another. He is able to wound the deathclaw with punches and slices, but the blade then causes him to get stuck when the deathclaw knocks him against a car wreck. The deathclaw moves to attack the Ghoul; Maximus is barely able to reach them in time, decapitating the deathclaw with his blades. The Ghoul, terrified from the encounter, offers a gesture of thanks and then enters the Lucky 38. Maximus stays outside to battle against two more deathclaws which have emerged. Maximus initially manages to hold out against one of the deathclaws, slicing off two of its fingers; however, it then hits him with its tail, causing him to fly back all the way into Freeside, smashing through the gate protecting them from the deathclaws. Seeing what has happened, Maximus realizes that all of Freeside is now in danger from the deathclaws, just as one of the creatures appears right at the destroyed gate. ====[[The Strip]]==== In [[Freeside]], the deathclaws realize they can enter through the broken gate, and Maximus urges everyone to get behind him and inside the buildings. As Thaddeus and the Freesiders run away, Maximus discovers that his Ranger power armor has a weapons system, which he uses to blow up a deathclaw. Thaddeus runs into a shop with other Freesiders, where they watch Maximus use a jetpack system to leap into the air and fire another missile at a deathclaw. Thaddeus tries to get the Freesiders to help, but they are dismissive. Maximus continues to fight the deathclaws alone as more run from the Strip to Freeside. Maximus continues to fight the deathclaws, slicing off one creature's arm and using its own arm as a bludgeon to kill it, then throwing the arm into the [[King's School of Impersonation]]. The Freesiders continue to watch as Maximus finally kills the deathclaw with a missile, although he realizes he is now out of ammunition. The Freesiders still do not intervene, and even begin betting on how long they believe Maximus will last. Maximus kills another deathclaw by running it through with a metal pole. As Maximus is pinned down and attacked by another deathclaw, the creature is shot in the head, stunning it. Maximus looks up to see where the shot came from, finding that Thaddeus has taken up sniper support on a rooftop even after losing his arm, now using his foot to steady the rifle. As they give each other a thumbs up, Maximus is attacked by the deathclaw again as Thaddeus struggles to reload his rifle. Maximus manages to kill his attacker by ripping off its jaw, but his armor is left in critical condition. He begins to have flashbacks to his past in Shady Sands as his suit is attacked by the last few deathclaws. His [[Joseph (TV series)|father's]] last words to him, telling him he will be a good man, echo in his mind. He then climbs out of the suit despite Thaddeus yelling at him not to, arming himself with a pool cue and a roulette wheel as a shield. Though [[Shotgun Jeff]] is stirred to action by the realization that their defender is just a "kid," no one else takes action, causing Jeff to also stand down. Maximus stares down the deathclaw as the image of the [[Quintus|knight who rescued him from Shady Sands]] goes through his mind. As the deathclaw charges at Maximus, it is suddenly shot dead. Thaddeus tells him the shooter is at the [[Silver Rush]] behind Maximus, where an [[NCR Veteran Ranger]] has taken up a position with an anti-materiel rifle. As Maximus takes notice of the Ranger, the Ranger fires another shot that hits the last deathclaw in the head. The rest of the Ranger's battalion then marches around the corner, with [[Rodriguez|Captain Rodriguez]] commanding them. She relieves Maximus, who gratefully obliges. Some time later, Maximus walks back to Strip gate, where he sees and calls out to Lucy, and the two embrace. Soon, Lucy and Maximus enter the penthouse of the Lucky 38, where they see House's monitor displaying only a "Signal Lost" screen. As the two look over New Vegas and the forces of Caesar's Legion approaching from the distance, Lucy tells him that there will be a war and it will be her fault. Maximus simply tells her, "Welcome to the Wasteland." Unseen by the two, House appears for a split second on his monitor before vanishing again. ==Personality== {{Cleanup|refs, grammar}} [[File:The Beginning episode banner.jpg|thumb|250px]] Maximus is someone who needs something to believe in to keep him going. He is said to be someone who yearns to cling onto something powerful, such as the Brotherhood because it makes him feel more capable than he is on his own.[https://web.archive.org/web/20240404013830/https://www.fandom.com/articles/fallout-series-preview Fandom: Prime’s ‘Fallout’ Series Explores the Satirical Side of the End of the World (archived)] He will do anything to further the Brotherhood's goals of bringing law and order to the wasteland.[https://web.archive.org/web/20240000000000*/https://press.amazonstudios.com/us/en/press-release/prime-video-and-kilter-films-unveils-official-trai Amazon Studios: Prime Video and Kilter Films Unveils Official Trailer for Highly Anticipated New Series Fallout Starring Ella Purnell, Aaron Moten, Walton Goggins, and Kyle MacLachlan (archived)] He is experiencing internal conflict and is said to be someone who has a war going on within himself.[https://web.archive.org/web/20240307175615/https://www.moviefone.com/news/10-things-we-learned-at-the-fallout-press-conference/ Moviefone: 10 Things We Learned at the ‘Fallout’ Press Conference with Cast and Crew (archived)] His biggest fear is weakness and he seeks power as a means to shield himself from the violence and dangers of the Wasteland.[https://www.amazon.com/Fallout-Season-1/dp/B0CN4HV16N Amazon show description] Maximus has a tendency to think in the moment and not think critically in his situation or plan ahead. For instance disguising himself as Knight Titus rather than simply claiming he fell in battle, which leads to the assignment of his rival Thaddeus as Squire necessitating that he keep up the ruse. Or when he assumes that Lucy is to be executed in Vault 4 and he rushes to his power armor when she had simply been exiled. This could also be inferred from his belief that the Great War and its atomic bombings refers to the destruction of Shady Sands, and his misconceptions regarding sexual intercourse. He also displays poor charisma on multiple occasions, such as failing to convince a repairwoman to fix a part at a cheaper price, or to convince Thaddeus to work with him on his impersonation of Knight Titus, or trying to proposition Lucy. Despite holding up the Brotherhood's ideals, he admits his primary motivation for fighting for the Brotherhood is to 'hurt the people that hurt me', and displays an eagerness to escalate to violence. He deals with a lot of pent up anger as an initiate when doing latrine duties, refuses to de-escalate crossing paths with a pair of wastelander cannibals, and contemplates harming Thaddeus when he has been assigned his squire (under the guise of Knight Titus). While seeing Thaddeus grovel before him as squire, he reconsiders but continues to demean him with pointless tasks until Thaddeus reveals sorrow at Maximus' (informed) passing. However Maximus is still willing to attempt to murder Thaddeus, crushing his foot, when he fails to convince Thaddeus to maintain the fiction of his assumed identity, despite both having saved the others life in an encounter with a Gulper. Perhaps correspondingly when shown the comfort, safety, and relative luxury of Vault life in Vault 4, he becomes willing to settle down and integrate into the community, abandoning his post with the Brotherhood and his mission. However, when he thinks that Lucy's life is in danger he goes to intervene knowing that he will no longer be able to stay in Vault 4. He likewise displays a callousness to the survival of Vault 4 having stolen their Fusion Core and wanting to keep it to maintain his T-60 Power Armor after having been banished from the Vault, but Lucy still manages to convince him to return it. However Maximus also demonstrates an altruistic side, idealizing Brotherhood knights and their role in protecting the wasteland and being gravely disappointed by Knight Titus being unable to meet that standard. He intervenes when seeing one wastelander trying to kill a snake oil salesman, and releases him when the confrontation passes. He also steps in to save Lucy from the Ghoul in Filly, shielding her with his power armor. Unlike most in the Brotherhood, Maximus is still sympathetic towards non-feral ghouls, who are blanket targeted and dehumanized by his chapter's core teachings. When he encounters feral ghouls in a [[shadowy facility]], he remorselessly guns them down without hesitation.
